name: interpret_channel_command_stream
description: Reads bytes from a per-channel stream: values below 240 are handled as data entries that index a table and advance the position, while larger values select one of sixteen handlers by their low four bits. The handlers cover jumps, loops, channel setup and the early return path, and the routine calls itself recursively for nested entries.

name: advance_index_and_clear_slot
description: Marks one channel slot as idle with an all-ones byte, then advances a two-word index that wraps back to its start value once it reaches its limit. It then calls a further routine and sets a flag byte to 255 before returning.

name: bump_counter_and_mark_done
description: Increments a 16-bit counter held in the caller's structure, calls a further routine, and then sets a completion byte to 255 before returning.

name: dispatch_sequence_command_bytes
description: Handles the same channel command stream as its neighbour, with the entry point moved to a different starting label. It reads the command byte, adjusts the position counter and either returns, jumps to a handler, or continues reading.

name: mark_channel_slot_idle
description: Sets one byte in the caller's channel structure to 255 and returns, which marks that channel slot as inactive.

name: load_six_word_channel_row
description: Reads a row of six 16-bit values from a pattern table, indexed by the current step. If the first word is a fixed sentinel it dispatches to a handler chosen by the next word; otherwise it stores each value into its channel field and sets the matching active flag when the value is non-negative.

name: clear_channel_status_byte
description: Writes zero to one status byte in the channel's frame structure and returns. It is a one-instruction clear.

name: step_and_load_channel_row
description: Advances the channel's step counter and, on the first pass only, initialises a pair of state bytes from the data pointer. It then reads a row of six 16-bit values from the pattern table and stores them into the channel fields, dispatching on a sentinel word as the neighbouring loader does.

name: clear_channel_status_flag
description: Writes zero to one status byte in the channel's frame structure and returns. It has the same one-instruction body as its sibling clearing routine.

name: update_voice_envelopes_and_output
description: Runs the per-frame sound update: it calls three helper routines, then steps several pitch and volume slides, applies a frequency and scale correction, and writes the results to output words. When a sample pointer is active it fills an output buffer byte by byte from a table, adding a running delta.

name: advance_channel_wave_tick
description: Steps one channel's pitch and level slides and, while its wave is active, fills an output buffer from a byte table using a running delta. It counts down envelope and repeat counters and flips their signs when they reach zero.

name: update_voice_wave_with_interrupts
description: Performs the same per-voice wave and slide tick as its sibling, stepping pitch and level counters and copying table bytes into an output buffer. Its hardware references include the interrupt enable and request registers, so it probably masks interrupts around the update.

name: reset_voice_fields_and_dispatch
description: Clears several per-voice fields and advances the step index, then reads the next command word from the channel table. A zero command byte dispatches through a handler table; otherwise the routine decrements a repeat counter and ORs a mask into a status word.

name: dispatch_next_channel_command
description: Copies a stored argument into a state word, merges a channel mask into a status word, advances the step and reads the next command byte. It then dispatches to the matching handler through a table.

name: set_channel_base_and_dispatch
description: Clears a per-channel flag and adds two stored values, writing the sum to the channel's position field and to a caller-supplied pointer. It then advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: store_argument_word_and_dispatch
description: Copies an argument word from the command data into two channel fields, advances the step and dispatches the next command through a table.

name: copy_argument_then_dispatch
description: Copies an argument word into a channel field, advances the step and reads a flag byte that is then set to 255. If the old flag was negative it returns early, otherwise it dispatches the next command.

name: repeat_count_step_and_dispatch
description: Manages a repeat counter: when it is zero it is set to 255 and the step advances, otherwise it is decremented or reloaded from the argument when it sits at the sentinel. The step is then set from the argument word and the next command is dispatched.

name: clear_channel_pointer_byte
description: Writes zero to the single byte that the channel pointer designates and returns. It is a one-byte clearing stub.

name: lookup_scaled_pitch_and_dispatch
description: Looks up a 16-bit pitch value from a fixed table at an index built from a channel offset and a command argument. It scales that value by a volume-like factor, stores it into the channel's pitch field, advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: lookup_pitch_and_dispatch
description: Looks up a 16-bit pitch value from a fixed table at an index taken from the command argument, scales it by a stored factor when the factor is non-zero, and stores it in the channel's pitch fields. It advances the step, marks a flag byte as 255, and dispatches the next command when that flag was non-negative.

name: reset_channel_effects_and_dispatch
description: Clears five per-channel effect fields and advances the step, then reads the next command word from the channel table. The command is dispatched through the handler table.

name: set_effect_rate_and_dispatch
description: Stores an argument byte and half of that value as a rate and depth pair, and sets a flag byte to 1. When a pending value is zero it copies the current pitch into the channel's base field, then advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: compute_triple_offset_and_dispatch
description: Stores a byte made from an argument plus three times a channel field, advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: store_argument_byte_and_dispatch
description: Copies one argument byte from the command data into a channel field, advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: store_four_argument_bytes
description: Copies four argument bytes from the command data into four channel fields, advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: hold_counter_step_and_dispatch
description: Manages a hold counter for the channel: a zero flag advances the step at once, while a set flag counts the hold down or reloads it from the argument. The step is then taken from the argument word and the next command is dispatched.

name: init_channel_position_and_dispatch
description: Clears a channel flag, copies a stored position value into two channel words and sets two counters to 1. It then advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: clear_pointer_byte_and_dispatch
description: Writes zero to the byte the channel pointer designates, copies a channel word into a global, and advances the step. It sets a flag byte to 255 and dispatches the next command when that flag was non-negative.

name: sum_base_offset_and_dispatch
description: Clears a channel flag and adds an argument to a stored base value, writing the sum to two channel fields and to a pointer offset by a channel word. It advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: set_half_length_and_dispatch
description: Stores half of an argument-derived value, treating zero as 256, into one channel field. It also writes a masked count and a second argument word into two more fields, then advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: store_shifted_argument_and_dispatch
description: Stores the command argument shifted left by eight bits into a channel field, advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: store_argument_pair_and_dispatch
description: Copies one argument word into two channel fields and a second argument word into a third, advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: store_long_argument_and_dispatch
description: Stores a 32-bit argument into a channel field, advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: store_three_argument_words
description: Copies argument words into three channel fields, advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: store_scaled_argument_and_dispatch
description: Stores an argument byte shifted left by four bits into one channel field and copies argument words into two more. It advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: clear_effect_fields_if_flagged
description: Advances the step and, when the argument byte is non-zero, clears twelve channel effect fields. It then reads the next command and dispatches it.

name: advance_step_and_dispatch_dma
description: Advances the channel step and, when a flag byte is clear, reads the next command and dispatches it. The facts list DMA and interrupt control registers as touched, but the shown body is only the step and dispatch logic, so the DMA use lies in the handlers it reaches.

name: accumulate_argument_offset_and_dispatch
description: Stores an argument byte into two channel fields, then adds an argument word to a running offset and writes the result to a stored pointer or position field. It advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: clear_pointer_and_write_intena
description: Clears the byte the channel pointer designates and copies a channel word into a global that the facts show is linked to the interrupt enable register. It advances the step and dispatches the next command when a flag was non-negative.

name: select_channel_record_by_status
description: Chooses one of four channel records by testing three status bits in a shared word, then copies a word from that record into the shared registers and marks the record's first byte as 255. Its facts list interrupt enable and request registers, with their read-back copies, as touched.

name: branch_on_argument_and_dispatch
description: Compares the argument byte with a channel threshold field. A smaller argument loads the argument word as the new step, otherwise the step advances, and the next command is then read and dispatched.

name: countdown_step_and_dispatch
description: Counts down a channel's repeat counter: a clear counter is armed to 255 and the step advances, while a set counter is decremented or reloaded from the argument. The step then comes from the argument word and the next command is dispatched.

name: set_flag_and_dispatch
description: Sets a channel flag byte to 255, advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: set_count_and_reload_step
description: Stores the argument byte minus one into a counter field, sets the step from the argument word and dispatches the next command.

name: gated_countdown_and_dispatch
description: Checks a gate byte first: when it is clear the step only advances. When it is set, a countdown flag is armed once to 255, then counted down or reloaded from the argument, and the step is taken from the argument word before the next command is dispatched.

name: lookup_pitch_index_and_dispatch
description: Looks up a pitch value from a fixed table at an index built from a channel offset and the argument, scales it by an argument-derived factor and stores it in the channel's pitch fields. It sets a flag to 255 and dispatches the next command when the old flag was non-negative.

name: store_argument_word_if_gated
description: Stores an argument word into a channel field and, when a gate word is zero, also copies it into a second field. It advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: clear_effect_block_and_dispatch
description: Clears five channel effect fields, advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: store_scaled_argument_pair
description: Stores one argument byte into a channel field and an argument byte shifted left by four bits into another. It also copies an argument word into two fields, then advances the step and dispatches the next command.

name: handle_channel_special_command
description: Selects a channel record from the low nibble of the command word and handles special command bytes: a marker stores a word and a flag, one value clears a status byte, and values above a threshold latch a new pitch from the table. Any other value is recorded as the channel's current note and marks the channel active; its facts also list DMA and interrupt enable registers.

name: update_level_direction_flag
description: When the second input byte is non-zero and the stored level differs from the new one, it records a direction of 1 or minus one and marks a pending update. Otherwise it stores the new level, clears the pending flag and sets the direction to zero.

name: reset_envelope_state
description: Copies one counter byte in the channel block into a second byte, clears a flag byte and zeroes a 16-bit field.

name: clear_channel_envelope_fields
description: Zeroes a status byte, a longword at offset 60 and a word at offset 94 in the channel block.

name: init_audio_channel_volumes
description: Clears two shared state words, calls four helper routines, then writes fixed values into the audio channel state and a control word. Its hardware references include the four audio volume registers and the DMA and interrupt control registers.

name: store_flagged_word_and_call
description: ORs the argument word with 256, stores the result in a shared word and calls a helper routine.

name: update_channel_pointers_from_table
description: Updates the channel's table pointers from a 32-entry word table indexed by a field of the channel, saving the previous selection in a second table and clearing several pending words. Its facts show the audio control register and the port A register that carries the fire button and disk status bits.

name: load_boot_segment_then_jump
description: Allocates memory through the exec library, fills an I/O request with a destination address and a fixed read length, and repeats the read until its completion flag clears. It then forbids multitasking, enters supervisor state and jumps into the loaded code.

name: load_second_boot_segment
description: Performs the same allocate, read and jump sequence as its sibling, with a shorter fixed read length. It uses the exec library calls for allocation, I/O, multitasking control and supervisor state.

name: setup_copper_display_list
description: Writes display window and data fetch limits, bitplane modulo and colour registers, then fills a copper list in memory with bitplane pointer moves and starts the copper on it. It runs during the boot block load to set up the screen.

name: wait_for_flag_and_result
description: Repeatedly calls a helper and waits while the low bit of a shared flag is set, until the helper returns 1.

name: set_timer_control_values
description: Writes three fixed control values, 8, 204 and 2, to the shared control word in turn and returns. The facts list CIA timer, colour and interrupt registers as touched by the wider routine.

name: decode_packed_block_header
description: Compares a value returned by a helper with a fixed signature constant, then runs a bit-level decode loop over the packed data using the shared reader helpers.

name: copy_back_reference_block
description: Copies a run of already-written output from an earlier position in the buffer to the current write position, stepping the destination pointer backwards through the buffer as it copies.

name: decode_bit_count_run
description: Entry fragment of the bit-level decoder: it shifts an input byte left through the extend flag to build a count, then loops while a counter word counts down and copies output when it reaches the end.

name: decode_extended_bit_tail
description: Loop tail of the bit-level decoder that doubles a counter word and merges in the extend flag, then copies output once the counter reaches its end value.

name: decode_extended_bit_pair
description: Bit-level decoder fragment that loads an input byte, updates the extend flag from its carry and shifts the next byte when the flag is set.

name: decode_marked_bit_run
description: Bit-level decoder fragment that checks a counter against the value 9 as a marker and keeps shifting input bytes until the marker is reached, then copies the result.

name: decode_flagged_bit_run
description: Bit-level decoder fragment that shifts input bits through the extend flag and reads a further input byte when the shifted value becomes zero.

name: decode_doubling_bit_run
description: Bit-level decoder fragment that doubles a counter word, combines it with the extend flag and reads a new input byte when the shifted byte is zero.

name: decode_carry_bit_run
description: Bit-level decoder fragment that tests the extend flag and shifts a pair of input bytes, branching to the copy step as the flag dictates.

name: decode_word_output_bit_run
description: Bit-level decoder fragment that doubles a counter word into a longer value, writes it out as a word and continues the copy loop.

name: decode_bit_literal_fragment
description: Fragment of a bit-level decoder that shifts a control byte through the carry, reads a new input byte when the control bits run out, and builds a count word from the bits.

name: decode_variable_length_count
description: Decodes a variable-length count from the bit stream by shifting the control byte through the carry, building two count words, and calling helper routines that copy the bytes described by each count.

name: copy_byte_pairs_then_decode
description: Copies byte pairs from the input pointer to the output pointer for a counted number of pairs, then resumes the bit-level decode loop.

name: decode_literal_bytes
description: Reads an input byte, shifts it through the extend flag, and copies the following bytes to the output as literals until the flag clears.

name: build_count_with_flag_bit
description: Builds a count word from shifted bits with a fixed flag bit ORed in, then calls helpers that use the count as the length of the next copy.

name: decode_extended_flag_entry
description: Entry fragment of the bit-level decoder: it reads a control byte, updates the extend flag and loops while the flag is set.

name: decode_extended_flag_test
description: Decoder fragment that reads a control byte, updates the extend flag from its carry and skips ahead while the flag is clear, counting the bit run.

name: decode_zero_check_run
description: Decoder fragment that reads a control byte and, when the extend flag is set, checks the following input byte for zero before choosing the next copy path.

name: decode_flagged_count_fragment
description: Decoder fragment that builds a count word with the fixed flag bit set and advances through the input bits as it goes.

name: decode_extended_bit_loop
description: Decoder fragment that reads a control byte, updates the extend flag and loops over input until the flag is clear.

name: decode_bit_shift_pair
description: Decoder fragment that shifts the control bits and fetches a new byte when they run out, then selects the next input pointer.

name: concatenate_two_longwords
description: Combines two 32-bit values into one 64-bit result, with the second value forming the high half.

name: accumulate_32bit_from_bytes
description: Reads four consecutive bytes from a pointer and builds a 32-bit value by shifting each byte into the result.

name: start_loaded_program_entry
description: Writes a set-enable value to the DMA control register, then clears all DMA and interrupt bits before calling a helper. The helper's result decides whether the routine spins forever or calls the loaded program's entry pointer; its facts also list the CIA port B and colour registers.

name: call_loaded_entry_point
description: Calls through the loaded program's entry pointer and returns.

name: compute_track_sector_position
description: Computes a track and sector position by dividing a block number by eleven, the sector count of a standard Amiga track, then calls helpers to set up that sector.

name: read_longword_after_blitter_wait
description: Calls helper routines, including the blitter wait routine, and returns the longword stored at a fixed offset from the frame pointer.

name: write_track_sector_headers
description: Writes disk sector headers into the track buffer by clearing per-sector fields and writing the standard MFM sync and preamble words before each sector's data. It also waits for the blitter, and its facts list the disk status and interrupt request registers.

name: start_disk_dma_transfer
description: Starts a disk DMA transfer by loading the disk pointer and length registers, setting the disk control word and enabling DMA. It then waits in a loop on helper results and the disk status bits.

name: write_sync_gap_words
description: Writes a repeated MFM sync longword into the track buffer on each of eleven passes, calling helper routines between writes.

name: retry_sector_read_loop
description: Retries a sector read up to ten times, calling helper routines and checking a status flag on each pass. It returns zero on a successful read, or 24 when all attempts are used up.

name: validate_sector_header_fields
description: Checks that the header matches the expected track, that the sector number is below eleven and that a second field is below twelve. On success it stores a derived gap value and returns zero, otherwise it returns 27.

name: read_track_sector_data
description: Waits on helper results and a sync status to read the sectors of a track into the track buffer, stepping by a fixed per-sector stride. It returns zero on success and minus one on error.

name: verify_track_checksums
description: Compares two values returned by helper routines and returns 25 when they differ. It returns zero once a status bit is set or a stored counter matches, otherwise it keeps looping over the track fields.

name: return_minus_one_stub
description: Returns minus one without doing any other work.

name: empty_stub_routine
description: Does nothing and returns, with no memory, register or call references in its body.

name: set_flag_and_increment_counter
description: Sets one bit in a 16-bit word, chosen by the low five bits of a register, then increments a 16-bit counter stored next to it.

name: clear_table_entries
description: Writes zero to ten entries of a table, advancing a fixed stride of bytes between each write.

name: extract_high_byte_pair
description: Calls a helper for its 32-bit result and returns a value with the low word in the low half and the high byte of that result in the high half.

name: interleave_word_bits
description: Reads two consecutive words through a pointer and merges their alternating bits, taking the odd-position bits from the second word and the even-position bits from the first word shifted up by one.

name: pass_result_to_helper
description: Calls one helper for its 32-bit result and passes that result on to a second helper.

name: xor_checksum_ten_longwords
description: XORs ten consecutive longwords, starting eight bytes into the structure, and masks the result to alternating bits.

name: compute_xor_checksum
description: XORs a run of words starting at the input pointer, with the count derived from a length word, and returns the result masked to alternating bits.

name: fill_memory_pattern
description: Fills a block with an alternating-bit pattern, writing backwards from the end. The block size is chosen by a flag in the structure.

name: initialize_object_state
description: Calls a helper and derives three integers from its result and two output values, storing them at fixed offsets in the structure. It also writes two constant words and a derived word to the same structure.

name: set_object_transforms
description: Stores helper results into several fields of a structure, sets constant words and derives a short field from a call result. It also calls the blitter wait routine.

name: setup_blitter_registers_and_wait
description: Waits for the blitter, enables blitter DMA through the DMA control register and then writes fixed mask, modulo and fill values into the blitter registers.

name: update_top_bit_from_neighbour
description: Reads a byte and the byte before it. If the preceding byte's low bit is clear it sets the top bit, unless bit six is already set, in which case it leaves the byte alone; if the low bit is set it clears the top bit. It calls two helpers first.

name: update_top_bit_by_neighbour
description: Performs the same top-bit update as its sibling without the helper calls, setting or clearing the top bit of a byte from the low bit of the byte before it.

name: store_low_seven_bits
description: Stores the input byte with its top bit cleared at the target pointer.

name: prepare_disk_read_registers
description: Enables disk DMA, writes the standard MFM sync word, and sets the disk pointer and length registers from its arguments. The length value selects a read, so this is the setup used before a track transfer.

name: wait_for_disk_status_bit
description: Polls a status byte through a helper until one bit is set. It then writes two fixed disk control values and returns zero, or returns minus one if the wait ends without that bit.

name: set_global_flags
description: Writes 2 and then 16384 to the shared control word, overwriting the first value, and returns. The facts list the disk length and interrupt request registers as touched.

name: set_control_word_for_index
description: Writes 1024 to the shared control word, then, when a stored signed value is negative, writes an all-ones byte to it using a bit chosen from a stored index. Its facts list the audio control register as touched.

name: set_bit_in_global_flag
description: Computes a bit index from a stored 16-bit value plus three, then writes the input byte with that bit set to the shared control word. The facts list the CIA port B register as touched.

name: reset_global_flag
description: Writes 255 to the shared control word and calls two helper routines. The facts list the CIA port B register as touched.

name: update_table_entry
description: Reads a 16-bit entry from a table indexed by a structure field and calls a helper when the entry is negative. It then compares two 16-bit fields, repeats a helper call for the difference, and writes a register value back into the table before calling another helper.

name: wait_control_bit_then_clear
description: Loops up to 86 passes while a bit in the shared control word stays set, calling a helper on each pass. When the bit clears it zeroes an indexed table entry and returns zero; if the bit never clears it returns 30.

name: clear_indexed_table_entry
description: Clears one 16-bit entry of a table in the shared control area, chosen by an index stored in the structure, and returns zero.

name: update_ciab_prb
description: Calls a helper for a byte, clears bit one of it when a second returned value is non-negative, and stores the byte with bit zero forced on to the shared control word. It then calls another helper. The facts list the CIA port B register as touched.

name: update_ciab_prb_bit
description: Builds a bit mask from a stored value plus three and the shared control word, clears a second bit when a table flag is set, and returns the adjusted value. The facts list the CIA port B register as touched.

name: store_helper_result_to_global
description: Calls a helper and stores its result in the shared control word. The facts list the CIA port B register as touched.

name: wait_until_helper_returns_one
description: Repeatedly calls a helper and waits while the low bit of a shared flag is set, until the helper returns 1. The facts list the CIA timer control register as touched.

name: set_timer_control_if_idle
description: When the shared flag bit is clear and the argument is not one, writes the timer control values 8, 204 and 2 to the shared control word.

name: set_ciab_timer
description: Writes the three timer values 8, 204 and 2 to the shared control word in sequence. The facts list the CIA timer registers as touched.

name: decode_packed_stream_entry
description: Top-level entry of a packed-data decoder for the second disk segment. It calls three helpers and then runs a bit-level decode loop that uses the shared reader routines.

name: copy_back_reference_longs
description: Copies longwords from an earlier position of the output buffer to the current write position, stepping backwards through the buffer, and calls one helper.

name: decode_bit_count_loop
description: Bit-level decoder loop that shifts input bytes through the extend flag, doubles a counter word and loops until the count reaches its limit.

name: decode_word_counter_fragment
description: Decoder fragment that shifts an input byte through the carry into a 16-bit counter, then continues the bit loop.

name: decode_flag_test_fragment
description: Decoder fragment that reads an input byte, updates the extend flag from its carry and returns to the bit loop while the flag is clear.

name: decode_bit_literal_loop
description: Decoder fragment that shifts an input byte through the extend flag to build a counter, then loops over the output as the bit reader requires.

name: decode_carry_bit_entry
description: Entry fragment of a bit-level decoder that reads an input byte, builds a count from its bits and updates the extend flag from the carry.

name: decode_doubling_counter_loop
description: Decoder loop that doubles a counter word, merges in the extend flag and keeps reading input bits until the counter is complete.

name: decode_word_doubling_loop
description: Decoder loop that shifts input bytes through the carry and doubles a 16-bit word on each pass, copying output when the word is finished.

name: decode_counter_word_loop
description: Decoder fragment that runs a counter word through the extend flag and copies a run of output when the counter is complete.

name: build_three_step_counter
description: Builds a count from three bit shifts of a control byte, reading the next input byte whenever the control byte runs out.

name: decode_length_code_sequence
description: Decodes a sequence of length codes from the bit stream, calling helper routines that copy the bytes each code describes.

name: copy_word_pairs_then_decode
description: Copies word pairs from the input pointer to the output pointer for a counted number of pairs, then resumes the bit-level decode loop.

name: decode_literal_run_fragment
description: Decoder fragment that copies input bytes to the output as literals, two at a time, until the counter reaches its end.

name: decode_bit_flag_step
description: Decoder step that reads a bit flag from the control byte and shifts the next input byte when the flag is set.

name: decode_carry_check_fragment
description: Decoder fragment that tests the carry of a shifted input byte and branches to the copy step accordingly.

name: decode_extended_flag_loop
description: Decoder loop that reads an input byte, updates the extend flag from its carry and continues while the flag remains set.

name: decode_bit_pair_fragment
description: Decoder fragment that shifts a pair of control bits and branches to the copy step when the shifted value is zero.

name: decode_word_doubling_fragment
description: Decoder fragment that doubles a 16-bit counter word, adds the extend flag and reads a new input byte when the shifted byte is zero.

name: decode_pair_shift_fragment
description: Decoder fragment that shifts a pair of input bytes through the carry and copies the result to the output.

name: decode_bit_shift_chain
description: Decoder fragment that shifts control bits in sequence and fetches a new input byte when they run out, then selects the next input pointer.

name: combine_longword_pair
description: Combines two 32-bit values into one 64-bit result, with the second value forming the high half.

name: read_longword_from_bytes
description: Reads four consecutive bytes from a pointer and builds a 32-bit value by shifting each byte into the result.

name: start_second_program_entry
description: Sets the shared control word, writes DMA and interrupt disable masks, calls a helper and then calls the loaded program's entry pointer. The helper result can send the routine into an endless loop; its facts list the CIA port B, colour, DMA and interrupt registers as touched.

name: call_second_entry_point
description: Calls through the second loaded program's entry pointer and returns.

name: compute_track_sector_offsets
description: Derives a track and sector position from a block number by dividing by eleven, the sector count of a standard Amiga track, and checks the result against a limit. Helper routines then set up that sector.

name: read_longword_after_helpers
description: Calls two helper routines and returns a 64-bit value: the high half from the helper's register result and the low half from a longword stored in the frame.

name: verify_track_sector_headers
description: Clears per-sector fields and checks each sector header through helper routines, retrying up to four times. Its facts list the disk status port and the interrupt request read-back register as touched.

name: start_disk_dma_read
description: Starts a disk DMA transfer by writing the disk pointer and length registers and the disk control word, then polls helper results and the disk status bits. It returns a status code of 28 when the transfer does not complete.

name: write_sync_gap_longs
description: Writes a repeated MFM sync longword into the track buffer on each of eleven passes, calling helper routines between writes.

name: retry_header_check_loop
description: Retries up to ten times, calling helper routines and checking a status flag each time. It returns the helper's result when the flag is clear, or 24 when all attempts are used up.

name: check_sector_header_match
description: Checks a header against the expected track value, that a sector number is below eleven and that a second field is below twelve. On success it stores a derived gap value and returns zero, otherwise it returns 27.

name: return_status_code_24
description: Returns the status code 24 without doing any other work.

name: return_status_code_27
description: Returns the status code 27 without doing any other work.

name: return_status_code_25
description: Returns the status code 25 without doing any other work.

name: read_track_sector_bytes
description: Waits on helper results and a sync status to read the sectors of a track into the track buffer, stepping by a fixed per-sector stride. It returns zero when the read completes and otherwise returns a status code.

name: verify_track_checksum_pass
description: Compares two values returned by helper routines and returns 25 when they differ. It returns zero once a status bit is set or a stored counter matches, otherwise it keeps looping over the track fields.

name: return_minus_one_status
description: Returns minus one without doing any other work.

name: empty_stub_routine
description: Does nothing and returns, with no memory, register or call references in its body.

name: set_flag_and_increment_counter
description: Sets one bit in a 16-bit word, chosen by the low five bits of a register, then increments a 16-bit counter stored next to it.

name: clear_table_entries
description: Writes zero to ten entries of a table, advancing a fixed stride of bytes between each write.

name: extract_high_byte_pair
description: Calls a helper for its 32-bit result and returns a value with the low word in the low half and the high byte of that result in the high half.

name: interleave_word_bits
description: Reads two consecutive words through a pointer and merges their alternating bits, taking the odd-position bits from the second word and the even-position bits from the first word shifted up by one.

name: pass_result_to_helper
description: Calls one helper for its 32-bit result and passes that result on to a second helper.

name: xor_checksum_ten_longwords
description: XORs ten consecutive longwords, starting eight bytes into the structure, and masks the result to alternating bits.

name: xor_checksum_word_run
description: XORs a run of longwords, with the count derived from a length word, and returns the result masked to alternating bits.

name: fill_memory_pattern
description: Fills a block with an alternating-bit pattern, writing backwards from the end. The block size is chosen by a flag in the structure.

name: initialize_object_state
description: Calls a helper and derives three integers from its result and two output values, storing them at fixed offsets in the structure. It also writes two constant words and a derived word to the same structure.

name: set_object_transforms
description: Stores helper results into several fields of a structure, sets constant words and derives a short field from a call result. It also calls the blitter wait routine.

name: wait_for_blitter_idle
description: Spins while bit six of a shared status word is set, then returns. Its facts show it reads the DMA control read-back register, which carries the blitter busy bit.

name: write_blitter_fixed_registers
description: Calls a helper, enables blitter DMA through the DMA control register and then writes fixed mask, modulo and fill values into the blitter registers.

name: update_top_bit_from_neighbour
description: Reads a byte and the byte before it. If the preceding byte's low bit is clear it sets the top bit, unless bit six is already set, in which case it leaves the byte alone; if the low bit is set it clears the top bit. It calls two helpers first.

name: update_top_bit_by_neighbour
description: Performs the same top-bit update as its sibling without the helper calls, setting or clearing the top bit of a byte from the low bit of the byte before it.

name: store_low_seven_bits
description: Stores the input byte with its top bit cleared at the target pointer.

name: prepare_disk_read_registers
description: Enables disk DMA, writes the standard MFM sync word, and sets the disk pointer and length registers from its arguments. The length value selects a read, so this is the setup used before a track transfer.

name: wait_for_disk_status_bit
description: Polls a status byte through a helper until one bit is set. It then writes two fixed disk control values and returns zero, or returns minus one if the wait ends without that bit.

name: set_global_flags
description: Writes 2 and then 16384 to the shared control word, overwriting the first value, and returns. The facts list the disk length and interrupt request registers as touched.

name: set_global_flags
description: Writes 2 and then 16384 to the shared control word, overwriting the first value, and returns. The facts list the disk length and interrupt request registers as touched.

name: set_control_word_for_index
description: Writes 1024 to the shared control word, then, when a stored signed value is negative, writes an all-ones byte to it using a bit chosen from a stored index. Its facts list the audio control register as touched.

name: set_bit_in_global_flag
description: Computes a bit index from a stored 16-bit value plus three, then writes the input byte with that bit set to the shared control word. The facts list the CIA port B register as touched.

name: reset_global_flag
description: Writes 255 to the shared control word and calls two helper routines. The facts list the CIA port B register as touched.

name: update_table_entry
description: Reads a 16-bit entry from a table indexed by a structure field and calls a helper when the entry is negative. It then compares two 16-bit fields, repeats a helper call for the difference, and writes a register value back into the table before calling another helper.

name: wait_control_bit_then_clear
description: Loops up to 86 passes while a bit in the shared control word stays set, calling a helper on each pass. When the bit clears it zeroes an indexed table entry and returns zero; if the bit never clears it returns 30.

name: clear_indexed_table_entry
description: Clears one 16-bit entry of a table in the shared control area, chosen by an index stored in the structure, and returns zero.

name: update_ciab_prb
description: Calls a helper for a byte, clears bit one of it when a second returned value is non-negative, and stores the byte with bit zero forced on to the shared control word. It then calls another helper. The facts list the CIA port B register as touched.

name: store_helper_result_to_global
description: Calls a helper and stores its result in the shared control word. The facts list the CIA port B register as touched.

name: update_ciab_prb_bit
description: Builds a bit mask from a stored value plus three and the shared control word, clears a second bit when a table flag is set, and returns the adjusted value. The facts list the CIA port B register as touched.

name: wait_until_helper_returns_one
description: Repeatedly calls a helper and waits while the low bit of a shared flag is set, until the helper returns 1. The facts list the CIA timer control register as touched.

name: set_timer_control_if_idle
description: When the shared flag bit is clear and the argument is not one, writes the timer control values 8, 204 and 2 to the shared control word.

name: set_ciab_timer
description: Writes the three timer values 8, 204 and 2 to the shared control word in sequence. The facts list the CIA timer registers as touched.

name: select_handler_by_status
description: Calls a routine through a pointer in the structure, then compares the result of a second call with two fixed sentinel values. A match stores a handler pointer and calls a further routine; otherwise it calls the entry stored in the structure's pointer table.

name: clear_low_memory_setup
description: Calls one routine through the structure, clears a block of low-memory longwords, and writes a series of fixed addresses and values into a shared location, calling a helper after each write. It also zeroes several state bytes and words, sets a flag byte to 255, and branches to a second setup sequence when a flag is set.

name: clear_block_and_set_fields
description: Calls a routine through the structure and stores its result in a field, clears a block of longwords and zeroes four state fields. It then sets a flag byte and calls a series of helpers, branching to a second sequence when a flag word is non-zero.
